questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the university was academically good, and that there were no language barrier (english speaking country).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked it, but I also had a lot of trouble in the proces.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Okay. Not EASY, but if you set aside time, it was ok.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of voluntary student greeted you and showed you your way to accommodation etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was a lot of information, but almost to a point where there was too much, which made it difficult to know where to turn.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A lot of different options. Campus is big.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could pay for a meal plan and get money on a card, where you payed in the different places on campus - both grocery stores, cafés, restaurants etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's is NOT pretty and even mouldy in Tennis Court at least. I would though definitely recommend getting accommodation on campus, because it's way harder to get friends if not. Also campus is much prettier. Maybe go for Mason Village though, because the price is not much higher, but the quality is.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They helped you along the way with zoom meetings. Pretty last minute, but it was okay.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Zoom meetings and mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a trouble, and I missed some valuable weeks, because the semester is so short. I did though get the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The semester is very short. Maybe see if you can sign a shorter lease, so you can spend money on the time you are there instead of on housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lower level than used to, but different style of teaching and assignments were more thesis-ish, than we are used to, which was a challenge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same. Less law-like I think. And more space for critique and reflection.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender and Law
Renewable Energy and Climate Change Law
International Dispute Resolution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Gender and Law! Really good course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: People want to travel europe, and you wanna join ;-) Save money for travelling around the UK as well as europe, so you can join your new friends - especially in breaks, which are very long (appr. a whole month), because everyone goes away to travel europe.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries, food and coffee less expensive
Trains around UK way more expensive than anticipated

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Literally everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for the gym and some social clubs (e.g. I was on a very ambitious dance team)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: London, Wales, Scotland, Worcester, Bath, Brighton, Oxford - many options.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You are not as funny in english, and can have a hard time finding your words in the beginning, so it is hard to "jump in"

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are more openminded to talk to strangers etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get proper housing ON CAMPUS (preferably with en-suite)
Talk to people and never say no to any plans
Save money for traveling all of europe

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Waterstones + books in general = <3 <3 <3
The semesters are not as long as stated on the website

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The administrative work in the beginning
Having more time than usual and feeling dependent on people wanting to hang out, because you cannot make as many plans alone, ad you usually can at home. Also it can get very lonely and sad sometimes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
